newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Repair work starts on crippled Colombia pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Repair work starts on crippled Colombia pipeline.

text.p: Engineers have begun repairing Colombia's crippled Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline but it will be at least Friday before it is fully operational, industry sources said Tuesday.
The pipeline, which serves the Cano Limon field operated by U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp, was blown up twice by leftist rebels and partially destroyed by a landslide over the weekend.

"Repair teams went in late Monday night to one section but haven't been authorized by the military to start work on the second dynamited section," a spokesman for the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.
"We working in the area hit by a landslide but that's the complicated part. We must stabilize the surrounding land and repair part of the road before we can work on the pipeline," he added.

Occidental shut in the field and declared force majeure on production early Monday in the wake of the pipeline ruptures. Ecopetrol declared force majeure on the transport of crude but has so far not decided on liftings and exports.

Ecopetrol was still refusing to say Tuesday how much crude was in the 2 million barrel capacity storage complex at the Caribbean lifting terminal at Covenas or what the near-term loadings schedule was.
